subject: URGENT: VoltCloud production 5xx/429 surge after modelv4f quant rollout
messages:
From: Pedro Alvarez <pedro@voltcloud.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: elena@voltcloud.com, ops@voltcloud.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: sudden 5xx/429 spike in production after last night deploy

Dylan —

We've been seeing a steep increase in 5xx and 429 responses starting ~13:45 UTC after the scheduled model rollout (modelv4f + new quant profile). Latency is up across our top routes (median p95 -> 780ms, 5xx rate ~4.2% last hour). Our clients are retrying aggressively and we're hitting client-side throttles.

Attached is a screenshot from Grafana and a few sample error responses. Can you confirm if Redwood pushed any kernel/quant changes to our tenant last night? This is affecting all traffic in us-east.

Please escalate — we need either immediate mitigation or a rollback window.

— Pedro

Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/429 spike in production after last night deploy

Folks — preliminary triage from runtime metrics and logs (attaching trimmed excerpts to internal runbook). Key findings:

- Error signature: repeated OOM/dispatcher-429 on kernels tagged with "quant-opt-v2" when sequence length > 512. 5xxs correlate with token-cache misses and immediate retry attempts that amplify concurrency.
- Scope: ~92% of affected requests hit modelv4f:quant-opt-v2. Other variants (modelv4e, modelv4f-reduced) show normal behavior.
- Root cause hypothesis: the new kernel's memory estimation is underreporting KV cache overhead at higher sequence lengths. Under load, this causes transient OOMs and the serving layer to return 5xx/429 while clients retry.

Immediate mitigations (recommend):
1) Disable quant-opt-v2 for VoltCloud tenant (server-side toggle) — stops the new kernel from being selected.
2) Apply routing rule to prefer modelv4e (stable) for the next 2 hours.
3) Temporarily reduce max concurrency per worker for this tenant to reduce retry amplification.
4) Increase 429->backoff header to encourage client-side exponential backoff (ask VoltCloud to apply if possible).

Action owner suggestions: Markus to flip kernel toggle; Dylan/Marissa to coordinate rollback and external comms; Soojin to monitor logs and KV cache metrics.

Short timeline: disable kernel (T+10m), route change (T+20m), confirm p95 & 5xx drop (T+40m).

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Staff, Serving Runtime (Redwood Inference)

All — I've executed the kernel toggle to disable "quant-opt-v2" for the VoltCloud tenant (change id: CHG-20261130-457). Routing rule to prefer modelv4e has been pushed (rule id: ROUTE-VC-091).

Initial metrics: within 12 minutes of the toggle, 5xx dropped from 4.2% -> 0.6% and 429s reduced by ~70%. p95 latency improved to ~300ms. We're keeping the reduced concurrency cap in place for 1 hour to observe.

Next steps:
- I'll stage a controlled rollback plan if the toggle isn't sufficient (rollback_playbook_v1.md attached).
- Soojin: please continue watching KV cache metrics and share any anomalies.
- Dylan/Marissa: please coordinate a customer-facing update and schedule an exec sync if VoltCloud wants it.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Runtime, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Update & next steps — VoltCloud incident (modelv4f quant kernel)

Hi Pedro / Elena —

Thank you again for flagging this so quickly. Short summary and current state:

- Incident: increased 5xx/429 and latency after modelv4f quant-opt-v2 became selectable for your tenant during last night's rollout.
- Mitigation applied: kernel toggle disabled and routing preference reverted to modelv4e. Change ids: CHG-20261130-457, ROUTE-VC-091.
- Impact: 5xxs are back to baseline (0.5–0.8%) and latency p95 is down to ~320ms. We are keeping conservative concurrency caps for a monitoring window of 2 hours.

Planned follow-ups:
1) Deep RCA: Soojin and Runtime team will correlate memory estimation vs actual KV cache footprint across sequence length buckets and report back with root cause and long-term fix ETA (expected preliminary RCA in 48–72 hours).
2) Safeguards: We will add a tenant-level canary gate for future kernel rollouts (auto-disable if error rate exceeds 0.5% above baseline) and add sequence-length-aware memory checks to kernel selection logic.
3) Customer ops: Laura will reach out to schedule an exec sync this week to review impact and credits.

Attachments: trimmed runtime logs + rollback playbook + screenshot.

Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the partnership and will follow up with the RCA as soon as it's available.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
